$comment: The SPEC.md §3.1 capability map, in the one machine-readable form the toolchain reads.
tools/eslint-rules/module-boundaries.js enforces it; nothing duplicates it.
Adding a module here does NOT create it — it declares what that module is allowed to import.
An import not permitted by this file is a lint error naming both modules, so widening a
module's reach is a deliberate edit to this table and shows up in review as one.
Arrows point one way. SPEC.md §3.1 states the graph is acyclic; `pnpm lint` proves it, because
the rule refuses to load a graph containing a cycle.
Modules realized under apps/api/src/modules/ are the ones the rule can actually see. The
later-phase entries are recorded so the table stays the single description of the map.

business-approval.$comment: The approval-owned Visit C hard gate is the only component allowed to enqueue booking instructions, so messaging is an explicit dependency.

reservation.$comment: Visit A owns reservation extraction and participant corrections, so campaign normalization and messaging are explicit dependencies.

guideline-delivery.$comment: T87 composes a validated Visit A reservation into guideline delivery without allowing extraction evidence to bypass readiness.

admin-api.$comment: SPEC.md §3.1 says 'all business-flow modules, audit-log'. Enumerated, because a rule cannot read prose.

ocr-extraction.$comment: Phase 5 — unlocks Visit B and full Visit C.

operator-console.$comment: Realized as apps/admin (Milestone 3), not as an apps/api module, so the rule never sees it.
